newsitem.title: UK: Cold weather in Europe boosts oil price further.
newsitem.headline: Cold weather in Europe boosts oil price further.

text.p: Friday as winter chills swept across Europe and fresh data from the United States showed cold weather demand had eaten again into low inventory levels, traders said.
Benchmark Brent crude oil for February delivery traded on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) at $23.61 a barrel at 1335 GMT, 22 cents up from Tuesday's close.
"It is snowing outide the exchange and that is normally enough to encourage a bit of buying," one London-based trader said.

Fresh data released by the U.S. Energy Information Agency (EIA) and the American Petroleum Institute (API) late on Thursday showed a hefty 5-6 million barrel weekly fall in U.S. crude oil stocks levels, to around 290 million barrels.
These now stand roughly 20 million barrels below last year's levels, according to the two agencies.
U.S. stocks of heating oil also fell by 1.5-2 million barrels. While this is a relatively small amount, it had a positive effect on prices because traders had been expecting a rise in stocks.
Prices have been historically strong throughout this year because of low oil stocks, and this has injected an extra note of weather-sensitivity into prices.

"The current spate of cold weather entering Europe should support the IPE contracts and, to some extent, counteract the forecasts of warmer than expected weather in the U.S.," brokers GNI said in a daily report.
Prices have failed to decline significantly despite this month's signing of an oil-for-food deal between the United Nations and Iraq.

Iraqi oil is now flowing and the U.N. has so far approved 18 contracts for about 500,000 barrels a day of crude exports, enough at current prices for the $2 billion worth of sales Iraq is allowed over a six month period to pay for humanitarian needs.

"I think inventory levels, especially in the U.S., are still lean enough for the weather to be a key factor for a while yet, and stop Iraqi crude having a big impact," said Russell Hill, head trader at Austrian oil company OMV.
